title: Movement Patterns: Hinge & Squat

learn.summary: The hip hinge and the squat are the two lower-body patterns that carry you through life — picking things up and getting up and down. Master them with bodyweight before ever adding load: a clean pattern under no weight is worth more than a sloppy one under a barbell. Depth and control come from mobility as much as strength.

do: Film yourself from the side doing 5 bodyweight squats and 5 hip hinges today — watch it back and note one thing to fix.

children.title: The Hip Hinge

learn.summary: The hinge is hips back, flat spine, soft knees — the pattern behind deadlifts, kettlebell swings, and safely picking up anything heavy. Learn it with a dowel held against head, upper back, and tailbone: all three contact points stay touching as you fold. If the dowel leaves your low back, you're rounding.

do: Do 2 sets of 10 dowel (or broomstick) hinges maintaining three points of contact — daily for the next 3 days.

children.title: The Squat Pattern

learn.summary: A good squat: feet roughly shoulder-width, toes slightly out, knees tracking over toes, chest tall, weight mid-foot, hips below knee crease at the bottom. Toddlers do this perfectly; adults lose it from sitting in chairs. The deep resting squat is itself a mobility position worth reclaiming, not just an exercise rep.

do: Accumulate 2 total minutes in a deep bodyweight squat today, holding onto a doorframe or table for support if needed.

children.title: Ankle & Hip Mobility

learn.summary: Most squat-depth problems are ankle problems. Test: kneel with your big toe 5 inches (about 12 cm) from a wall and drive the knee to touch it without the heel lifting — failure means limited dorsiflexion. Fix with weighted knee-over-toe rocks and calf work; for hips, 90/90 transitions and deep lunge holds cover most of what you need.

do: Do the knee-to-wall ankle test on both sides today and record the max distance from the wall you pass at — retest in 4 weeks.

children.title: Loading the Patterns

learn.summary: Once bodyweight reps are clean, load conservatively: goblet squats and kettlebell deadlifts are the friendliest entry points because the front-held weight acts as a counterbalance that actually improves form. A sensible first milestone is a goblet squat with a third of your bodyweight for 10 reps. Progress load only when all reps look identical.

do: Do 3 sets of 8 goblet squats this week holding any single weight — a dumbbell, kettlebell, or loaded backpack.
